I have the file contents. I’m pulling line numbers so the findings are precise, then I’ll summarize the module and the concrete bugs.

**Findings**

1. [test/orders.js](/abs/path/C:/Users/Kerim/AppData/Local/Temp/codex-eco-bench-J014pF/test/orders.js:5) has an off-by-one loop bug in `calcTotal`. The loop uses `i <= items.length`, so the last iteration reads `items[items.length]`, which is `undefined`, and line 6 then throws when accessing `.price`. As written, `calcTotal` fails for any non-empty array, and even for an empty array.

2. [test/orders.js](/abs/path/C:/Users/Kerim/AppData/Local/Temp/codex-eco-bench-J014pF/test/orders.js:20) computes the wrong value in `averageItemPrice`. `calcTotal(items)` is a quantity-weighted order total, so dividing by `items.length` gives average line value, not average item price. Example: `{price: 10, qty: 10}` and `{price: 20, qty: 1}` returns `120 / 2 = 60`, but the average item price is not `60`.

3. [test/orders.js](/abs/path/C:/Users/Kerim/AppData/Local/Temp/codex-eco-bench-J014pF/test/orders.js:20) also has an empty-input bug. If `items.length === 0`, `averageItemPrice` returns `NaN` from `0 / 0` instead of handling the case explicitly.

Briefly, this module exports small order helpers: `calcTotal` sums `price * qty` across items, `applyDiscount` applies known percentage codes, `averageItemPrice` tries to derive an average from the items array, and `formatOrder` renders item lines plus a discounted total.

No changes made.
